description: K-12 edtech framework layer — SIS/gradebook schema (students, teachers, classes, assignments, submissions, grades, parent-student links), FERPA-aligned grade-read audit trail.

buildHints.whenToUse: K-12 school software: gradebooks, student information systems (SIS), roster management, assignment submission portals, or any product that stores student education records and must comply with FERPA.
firstSteps: Set DATABASE_URL to a Postgres connection string, then run `pnpm install && pnpm db:generate && pnpm db:migrate` to create all tables.
Start the server with `pnpm dev` — it listens on PORT (default 8103) and responds to GET /health immediately.
Seed a teacher row directly in Postgres, then POST /api/classes with the teacher's UUID as `teacherId`. All other routes flow from there.
Every call to GET /api/students/:id/grades writes a GradeAccessLog row before returning data — this is the FERPA audit trail. Do not remove or async-detach this write.
Run `pnpm validate` to verify the scaffold is wired correctly (checks schema tables, FERPA audit hook, /health route, valid package.json).
Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to typecheck — requires only `pnpm install` first, no build step needed.
dataModels: Student (districtStudentId, firstName, lastName, grade, enrolledAt, sisExternalId)
Teacher (districtStaffId, firstName, lastName, email, role: teacher|admin)
Class (code, title, subject, academicYear, term, teacherId)
GradeAccessLog (actorId, actorRole, studentId, assignmentId, accessedAt, reason)
integrations: SIS import adapter (OneRoster CSV / ClassLink / Clever — wire in src/sis/)

placeholders.description: {{port}} is replaced with the family default (8103) at compose time; falls back to the PORT env var at runtime. {{serviceName}} is replaced with the project slug (default: starter-foundry-k12).

architectureNotes: FERPA-aligned: every read of a grade writes a GradeAccessLog row before returning the grade
Parent access to a child's grades is gated by ParentStudent.canAccessGrades AND custodial-rights flag (not shipped; add before production)
Enrollments are soft-delete via droppedAt — historical grade lookups need the student on the roster at the time of assignment
gotchas: FERPA: student education records are protected. Every disclosure needs either parent consent (<18) or student consent (18+ / post-secondary). This scaffold does NOT implement consent tracking — add before production.

Directory information vs. education records: directory info (name, grade level, enrollment dates) CAN be disclosed without consent IF parents haven't opted out. Check district's annual directory-info policy.

Parent access is NOT automatic. Divorced / separated parents may have restricted custody — check custodial_rights before exposing a child's grades to a parent account. Missing this is a district lawsuit.
COPPA (under 13): collecting PII from students under 13 requires verifiable parental consent. Student accounts for K-7 need the parent consent flow, not direct signup.
State-level laws (e.g. California SOPIPA, New York 2-d) add requirements beyond FERPA. Check state before storing biometric data, location data, or behavioral tracking.
Don't log student names or grades into stdout/APM/error-tracking by default — redact in the logging middleware. A Sentry screenshot of a grade is a FERPA violation.
Grades are immutable once final; amendments are new rows with an `amendment_of_grade_id` FK, not UPDATEs. Preserves audit trail.
SIS imports are destructive: when OneRoster CSVs arrive, reconciliation must be idempotent and MUST NOT delete students silently — orphan detection should alert, not drop.
